title: Nitesh Tiwari
wiki_lead:
Nitesh Tiwari (born 22 May 1973) is an Indian film director, screenwriter, and lyricist known for his works in Hindi films. He debuted as a co-writer and co-director in Chillar Party (2011) which won him two National Film Awards, including Best Children's Film and Best Screenplay. He made his solo directorial debut with the supernatural political drama Bhoothnath Returns (2014).
Tiwari scripted and directed the highest grossing Indian film Dangal (2016), which was screened at the Beijing International Film Festival and the second BRICS festival. The film won him the Award for Best Director at the 62nd Filmfare Awards and the Telstra People's Choice Award at the 2017 Indian Film Festival of Melbourne. He followed up with the critically acclaimed coming-of-age film Chhichhore (2019), winning him a third National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi. Tiwari also directed the most expensive Indian film Ramayana: Part 1 (2026), based on the ancient Indian epic.
He co-founded Earthsky Pictures, producing ad films and the docu-series Break Point based on Indian tennis legends Mahesh Bhupathi and Leander Paes.

Tiwari scripted and directed the highest grossing Indian film Dangal (2016), which was screened at the Beijing International Film Festival and the second BRICS festival. He co-founded Earthsky Pictures, producing ad films and the docu-series Break Point based on Indian tennis legends Mahesh Bhupathi and Leander Paes.


Early life and education
Tiwari was born in Madhya Pradesh to B. D. Tiwari, who worked in the education department, resulting in the family moving every three years, and Twari did his schooling from different towns in Madhya Pradesh, including Ganj Basoda and Itarsi. He attended Bharat Mata Convent School at Ganj Basoda until class 8th, subsequently he attended a school in Vidisha, approximately 42 km away, as there were no English-medium schools in Gang Basoda at the time. For this he would cycle to Ganj Basoda railway station, along with other students, to travel to Vidisha.
He has a brother and a sister. He graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in 1996 with a bachelor's degree in Metallurgy and Material Science engineering. He worked as a creative director at Leo Burnett before entering Bollywood. He performed in a school play titled "Tapori-Mughal-e-Azam".


Career


2010s:
Tiwari began his filmmaking career with the 2011 feature Chillar Party. While serving as a creative director at Leo Burnett, Tiwari and co-writer Vikas Bahl, who was a creative head for UTV Spotboy, developed the screenplay as a collaborative project. Following a series of rejections from established directors who were reluctant to helm a film centered on a children’s ensemble, the pair chose to co-direct the project themselves, with UTV founder Ronnie Screwvala and actor Salman Khan producing the project. For his debut work, Tiwari received two National Film Awards, including Best Children's Film and Best Screenplay, solidifying his successful transition from advertising to feature filmmaking.
Following his debut, Tiwari transitioned to sole directorial duties for the 2014 supernatural political satire Bhoothnath Returns, a sequel to 2008's Bhoothnath; it marked the beginning of his association with fellow writers and future filmmakers Piyush Gupta

Born in Itarsi, Madhya Pradesh, he earned a B.Tech. degree in metallurgical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in 1996 before transitioning to filmmaking. Tiwari debuted as co-director with the children's film Chillar Party (2011), which earned the National Film Award for Best Children's Film. His subsequent directorial works include the comedy Bhoothnath Returns (2014), the biographical sports drama Dangal (2016) starring Aamir Khan, which grossed over â¹2,000 crore worldwide and set box office records as one of the highest-grossing Indian films, the dramedy Chhichhore (2019) that won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi, and the romantic drama Bawaal (2023). His films often blend emotional storytelling with commercial elements, achieving critical and commercial success, including Filmfare Awards for Best Director for Dangal.
